big: Dadi gets ₹10 lakh when her husband's job ends. She wants steady income, not a big risk. Which tools exist for her, and which are for other people?

lines: I am sixty-three and want regular money every quarter. What can I use?
The Senior Citizens Savings Scheme is made for that. Others, like Atal Pension Yojana and gratuity, are for different people at different times.

rows: Older people, with regular interest paid every quarter
Workers in the unorganised sector, for a fixed pension later
A lump sum from an employer after long service
A fixed amount paid from a mutual fund at intervals
note: Each tool has its own conditions and limits. Read the current terms before you commit.

title: Other pension tools
stops: SCSS pays regular interest to older people
Gratuity is paid by your bank
SWP takes a fixed sum from a fund at intervals
Atal Pension Yojana is for large companies only
caps: SCSS is a government-backed scheme that pays interest each quarter.
Gratuity comes from an employer, after years of service.
An SWP pays you a set amount, and the fund value changes.
Atal Pension Yojana is meant for workers outside formal pension cover.

q: Dadi wants a regular quarterly interest on a lump sum, from a government-backed scheme. What fits?
opts: A share of a small new company in the market
A gratuity from her former employer
why: A share of a small company is risky and pays nothing steady.
SCSS is built for older people, and pays interest every quarter.
Gratuity is an employer's lump sum and not a place to put savings.
Card rewards are not a source of retirement income.

q: Rohan leaves a company after many years of service. What may he receive from the employer?
opts: A refund of his tax paid
An SCSS account from the company
A home loan on easy terms
why: A tax refund is a separate matter between him and the tax office.
An employer does not open an SCSS account for a leaving employee.
A leaving employee is not owed a home loan by his old employer.
Gratuity is a lump sum paid by an employer after long service.

q: A retiree sets an SWP of ₹30,000 a month from a fund. What should she watch?
opts: Whether the fund can keep paying for many years
That the fund never changes in value at all
That the money is paid as a gift
That her SWP matches a friend's SWP
why: The fund value moves, so large draws may use up the pot sooner than planned.
Fund values do change, so expecting no change is a mistake.
An SWP is her own money coming back, not a gift.
Her need decides her SWP, and a friend's plan is no guide.

q: A domestic worker with no employer pension wants a fixed pension after 60. Which scheme is made for her?
why: SCSS is for people who are already sixty or older, and not for saving earlier.
Gratuity needs an employer who pays it, and she may have none.
Atal Pension Yojana is a government scheme for workers outside formal pension cover.
Rewards are not a pension and carry no promise of income.

pts: SCSS pays regular interest to older people, from a government-backed scheme.
Gratuity comes from an employer after long service.
An SWP pays a fixed sum from a fund, so watch how long the pot lasts.
